title: From The Good Earth to Lying Flat
subtitle: How the search for family security becomes accumulation, involution, and withdrawal
weight_semantics: Interpretive causal-emphasis units. Values express the relative importance of a pathway within this model; they are not survey estimates or population counts.

nodes.label: Scarcity memory
nodes.description: Historical memory of famine, dispossession, and insecure livelihood; the Good Earth baseline.

nodes.label: Reform-era growth bargain
nodes.description: Work, study, save, and defer gratification in exchange for upward mobility.

nodes.label: Property as family security
nodes.description: Housing becomes the urban successor to Wang Lung's land: store of value, marriage credential, and intergenerational insurance.

nodes.label: Credentials as mobility
nodes.description: Education becomes the principal route from family sacrifice to occupational security.

nodes.label: Consumption as proof of success
nodes.description: Brands, travel, technology, and lifestyle make reform-era advancement socially visible.

nodes.label: Housing-led accumulation
nodes.description: Savings, local finance, construction, and household expectations become tied to rising property values.

nodes.label: Credential arms race
nodes.description: More education is required to preserve the same relative position.

nodes.label: Status competition
nodes.description: Relative success matters more as consumption and achievement become publicly comparable.

nodes.label: Overwork as moral duty
nodes.description: Long hours are framed as deserved sacrifice for family advancement and national development.

nodes.label: Housing burden & wealth risk
nodes.description: High entry costs and falling or uncertain values weaken housing's promise of automatic security.

nodes.label: Graduate job mismatch
nodes.description: Credential growth outruns the supply of secure, high-status jobs.

nodes.label: Involution
nodes.description: Escalating effort produces little improvement in relative position or life chances.

nodes.label: Loss of future confidence
nodes.description: Households doubt that sacrifice today will reliably yield security tomorrow.

nodes.label: Precautionary saving
nodes.description: Households preserve cash and reduce discretionary spending in response to uncertainty.

nodes.label: Lying flat
nodes.description: Conscious reduction of career, consumption, and family ambitions as refusal of low-return competition.

nodes.label: Low-energy “rat people”
nodes.description: More private, aestheticized withdrawal into low-cost, low-energy domestic and online life.

nodes.label: Defensive stability seeking
nodes.description: Competition shifts toward civil-service posts, safe employers, cheap leisure, and other downside-minimizing choices.

nodes.label: Weak household consumption
nodes.description: Savings and withdrawal limit the consumption-led growth transition.

nodes.label: Delayed family formation
nodes.description: Housing, employment, and lifestyle uncertainty postpone marriage and childbearing.

nodes.label: Privatized retreat
nodes.description: Meaning shifts away from collective advancement toward small, controllable, low-cost private worlds.

edges.claim: Land/property is treated as protection against catastrophe.
Families diversify security from land into education.
Growth-era savings are capitalized into housing.
Educational sacrifice is justified by expected mobility.
Consumption makes achieved mobility visible.
Family security demand feeds housing-led accumulation.
The security asset also becomes an entry barrier.
Credential expansion raises the positional threshold.
Educational discipline normalizes sacrifice as virtue.
Visible consumption intensifies relative comparison.
Housing-centered growth raises purchase burdens and exposure to price shifts.
Property weakness damages the expected store of family wealth.
More graduates compete for fewer matching secure positions.
More effort is required to maintain the same rank.
Comparison turns absolute gains into relative inadequacy.
Visible success rewards conspicuous effort.
Sacrificial labor intensifies low-return competition.
Housing no longer guarantees an attainable or appreciating security anchor.
Housing costs and insecurity raise the threshold for marriage and children.
Underemployment makes additional effort feel positional rather than productive.
Credential-job mismatch weakens faith in the mobility bargain.
Some respond to low-return competition by consciously reducing ambition.
A smaller, stylized response is low-energy social and domestic withdrawal.
Others remain highly competitive but redirect effort toward safety rather than upside.
Uncertainty raises saving and debt reduction.
Low confidence reduces willingness to make long-horizon sacrifices.
Low confidence increases preference for protected or predictable careers.
Defensive saving suppresses discretionary demand.
Reduced career and status ambition lowers aspirational consumption.
Opting out includes postponing costly family milestones.
Agency is recovered through smaller, self-controlled lives.
The rat-person identity makes retreat socially legible and humorous.
Downside-minimizing households favor inexpensive and predictable consumption.
Life milestones wait until secure employment is obtained.
Stability seeking narrows life toward controllable institutions and routines.
